title: Determination 2023/039: Compliance of handrails to an external stair with Clause D1 Access routes
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Auckland Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992). Acceptable Solution D1/AS1 second edition, Amendment 6, effective 1 January 2017 (p.2 fn 5).

facts.text: The external timber stair leads to a deck and provides access to the main entrance of a single-storey dwelling whose floor level is higher than the surrounding ground.
The stair has two timber handrails, each 140 mm deep and 45 mm wide, bolted to the inside of 90 mm square posts, with 42 mm square balusters.

The building consent (granted 25 May 2023) covered replacing an existing deck and external stair. It named no clause D1 means of compliance, but an approved plan said the stair configuration was to be compliant with D1/AS1. The plans did not specify the handrail type, size, treatment or fixings.
On 9 August 2023 the authority's final inspection recorded: Handrail to be made graspable, does not comply with D1/AS1, relevant width exceeds 80mm.
The authority's 14 August 2023 letter cited D1/AS1 paragraphs 6.0.6-6.0.8 and Figure 26 and said the handrail must have a maximum graspable width of 80 mm.

The authority later said the stair was acceptable for the intent of the consent, then (21 September 2023) said that because the stair serves the main entry it needs a graspable handrail under D1/AS1 Figure 26.

The builder's submission: D1/AS1 is an acceptable solution only, its Figure 26 profiles are examples, the top of the rail is 45 mm wide, and the rail was installed upright so the top is graspable with at least 30 mm clear.
The matter to be determined under section 177(1)(a) is whether the two as-built handrails comply with clause D1.3.3(j), which requires smooth, reachable and graspable handrails.

D1/AS1 paragraph 6.0.8 gives a graspable profile as: flat or convex upper surface, arrised or radiused edges, minimum cross-section 20 mm, and a relevant width across the top surface of no more than 80 mm. Figure 26(a) shows some acceptable profiles, and others may also be acceptable.
Figure 26(b) (accessible stairs and ramps) is said not to apply because the stair is not required to be accessible under section 118.
